A.explanation: A zero horizontal force would require no horizontal pull at Y, but rod YZ at $30^{\circ}$ to the horizontal must exert a horizontal component on XY.

B.explanation: About $43 \text{ N}$ is $75 \text{ N} \times \tan 30^{\circ}$, which uses the wrong trigonometric ratio for the vertical equilibrium of rod YZ at Y.

C.explanation: The vertical component of the YZ force balances the $75 \text{ N}$ moment, giving $150 \text{ N}$ in YZ whose horizontal component of about $130 \text{ N}$ must be balanced by the wall at X.

D.explanation: $150 \text{ N}$ is the full force in rod YZ from $75 \text{ N} / \sin 30^{\circ}$, not its horizontal component acting on XY.

hints: Look at rod XY alone: the $75 \text{ N}$ sign pulls down at Y, $0.50 \text{ m}$ from the hinge at X, and rod YZ pulls up and left at Y at $30^{\circ}$ to the horizontal.

Take moments about the hinge X for rod XY so the unknown hinge forces have zero moment, leaving only the $75 \text{ N}$ clockwise moment and the anticlockwise moment from the vertical component of the YZ force.
First find the force in YZ from vertical balance of moments, then resolve that force horizontally with $\cos 30^{\circ}$ to find what the wall at X must balance for horizontal equilibrium.
walkthrough: Consider forces on the light horizontal rod XY. At Y there is $75 \text{ N}$ downward from the sign plus force $F$ from rod YZ acting along ZY, at $30^{\circ}$ above the horizontal.
For equilibrium, take moments about hinge X to remove the hinge forces. Clockwise moment is $75 \text{ N} \times 0.50 \text{ m}$.
The anticlockwise moment is only from the vertical component $F \sin 30^{\circ}$ times $0.50 \text{ m}$, because the horizontal component acts through the rod axis.
Set sum of moments to zero: $F \sin 30^{\circ} \times 0.50 = 75 \times 0.50$. Hence $F = 75 / \sin 30^{\circ} = 75 / 0.5 = 150 \text{ N}$.
Resolve $F$ horizontally at Y: $F_{x} = F \cos 30^{\circ} = 150 \times \cos 30^{\circ} \approx 150 \times 0.866 = 130 \text{ N}$ pulling XY toward the wall.
For horizontal equilibrium of XY, the wall hinge at X must push outward with equal magnitude, about $130 \text{ N}$. This is option C.
